messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: abnormal traffic spike detected for /v1/embeddings and /v1/generate. 90th p95 latency -> 800ms, 5xx rate up 2.5%. Bulk of requests appear to be non-authenticated or using recycled keys. Incident ID INC-2469123456 — paging oncall@sre

sasha: I'm on. seeing a huge fanout from ~120k rps to embeddings endpoints, also a smaller spike to chat/generate. traffic signature: high reqs with UA strings 'python-requests', 'okhttp', and 'curl/7' — looks like scraper cluster. geo: US/EU primarily. No single customer dominates. 429s climbing.

alex: taking pager. I'll join console. quick plan: 1) temporary global rate-slice on anonymous tier 2) quick WAF UA block for obvious scrapers 3) per-key throttles for noisy API keys 4) consider disabling batch-embeddings if load doesn't subside.

sasha: running quick checks — top IPs show bursty ephemeral ranges (likely compromised proxies). top request path breakdown: embeddings 62%, text-generate 28%, others 10%. KV cache hit rate unchanged — not cacheable requests.

ops-bot: ACTION: applied rate-slice policy 'anon-slice-50pct' -> reduced burst capacity for anonymous tier by 50%.

alex: OK ops-bot confirmed. Sasha, please add a WAF rule to block common UA patterns and apply a short TTL block to offending IPs. I'll prepare a customer notice template for paying customers.

sasha: adding waf rule now — running command:
```
redwoodctl waf add --name "scraper-ua-block-2469" --match-ua "python-requests|okhttp|scraper-bot|curl/7" --action block --ttl 3600
```

ops-bot: WAF rule 'scraper-ua-block-2469' added (id: waf-9f4). initial block hit: 74k requests/min matching rule. 5xx dropped ~18% after block applied.

alex: good. Next, per-key throttling: create a rule to cap unknown or new keys at 5 req/s and aggressively 429 after 50 concurrent requests. Sasha can you push?

sasha: pushing per-key throttle:
```
redwoodctl quota update --selector "key.age<7d OR key.tier==anon" --rate 5rps --burst 50 --action 429
```

ops-bot: Quota rule committed. Estimated reduction in throughput: ~40%. Observed 429s for flagged keys increasing as expected.

maya: support here — starting customer outreach. I'm drafting an in-product banner for affected logins and email to top 25 paying customers explaining: "We are experiencing elevated request volumes affecting embeddings throughput. We're actively mitigating and may temporarily reduce throughput for anonymous and new API keys. Paid customers are prioritized." Will post draft for review in 10m.

liam: flagged a subset of keys showing credential stuffing patterns — many keys rotated quickly, high reqs per second per key but valid signatures. Suggest we require CAPTCHA/JS challenge on signup and UI flows and consider forcing refresh for suspicious keys. Also recommend keeping WAF blocks for 2 hours and review logs for IP reuse.

alex: agree. For now do not revoke paying customer keys. If we find keys issuing abuse, we throttle. Liam, can you enable a fingerprint-based cap (UA+IP entropy) to reduce proxy evasion?

liam: will enable ephemeral fingerprint slice:
```
redwoodctl rate-slice add --name "fingerprint-slice-2469" --match "ua,ip_entropy" --ratelimit 2rps --duration 1800
```

ops-bot: Applied rate-slice 'fingerprint-slice-2469'. Early telemetry: additional 30% drop in ingress from identified clusters.

sasha: we still see embeddings load high from certain endpoints. considering disabling batch embeddings endpoint to free capacity for single embeddings for paying customers. thoughts?

alex: do it if load not trending down in 5m. Ensure we update API status page and CS templates first.

maya: ready to send notice once I get final wording. Draft: "We have applied temporary protections to limit automated traffic. If you see degraded embedding throughput, please reply to this thread and we'll prioritize. Expected mitigation window: 1-2 hours."

sasha: load trending down 45% overall after WAF+quota+slice. embeddings still 30% over baseline, but stable. I'll hold off on disabling batch endpoints for now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigation in progress, severity: high -> degraded. Current action list: WAF UA block, per-key throttles, fingerprint rate-slice, reduced anon burst.

alex: we should still gate batch embeddings as a contingency. ops-bot, can you stage a toggle?

ops-bot: batch-embeddings toggle staged: /feature/embeddings/batch -> off (warm standby). Ready to flip if requested.

liam: quick security note — observed credential stuffing indicators on auth endpoints for a small subset of customers. Not widespread but prioritize scans for exposed keys. I'll open a separate low-priority sec thread to track.

maya: sending CS notices now to top 25 customers and posting banner: 
```
[Banner] Elevated request volumes affecting embeddings. We are mitigating. Paid customers prioritized. Status page: https://status.redwood.example/INC-2469123456
```

ops-bot: Customer banner posted and email queued.

sasha: handoff: I'm at +45m oncall. Load is down ~55% from peak; 5xx rate back to baseline. Leaving WAF rule active and quota rules in place. If load spikes again, flip batch-embeddings off and escalate to infra for capacity. Handoff to alex for next 2h monitoring.

alex: taking handoff, will monitor dashboards and logs. @maya thanks — please keep CS thread open for any customer requests. @liam please follow with sec thread. I'll update postmortem owner and timeline.

liam: noted, I'll correlate IPs with existing abuse feeds and follow up. If we see repeated login attempts tied to a customer, we'll propose a forced rotation for that customer's API keys with outreach.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> degraded->monitoring. Mitigation start: 2469123462, primary throttle rules active, WAF rule active. Next: postmortem assigned to sasha, timeline 48h.

sasha: creating a quick runbook entry: what we did, commands used, rules' IDs, and unwind playbook. Will attach logs to the postmortem.

alex: closing active paging. Oncall note: leave waf-9f4 and fingerprint-slice-2469 active for 2h, then evaluate rollback with phased unwind. Postmortem to include customer impact summary and whether batch-embeddings toggle should be considered permanent for anonymous tier.

maya: I'll sync with account leads to confirm no paying customers were rate-limited. so far no inbound support tickets from top customers.

ops-bot: Summary metrics since mitigation: ingress down 62%, 5xx down to baseline, 429s account for most rejected traffic. Estimated service impact window finished for core paying flows.

alex: thanks team. Closing thread; follow-ups in PM. :white_check_mark:
